backgrounds: Single, unchanging set for the entire episode: a cozy stop-motion living room with a beige/cream sofa in the foreground where two characters sit side by side. Behind them is a softly blurred domestic backdrop featuring a floor lamp with a warm glowing shade, tall curtained windows, a wooden side table/console with small decorative objects (picture frames, a plant), and warm ambient wall tones. The camera holds one static medium shot on the couch for the whole runtime (no cuts to other locations), with the background kept in soft focus so attention stays on the two foreground characters. Title/intro cards appear as plain black frames with text, bookending the live-action-style scene.
props: Smartphones (each character holds one, screens lit, main focus of the physical comedy)
Beige/cream sofa with visible armrest and cushions
Floor lamp with warm lit shade in the background
Wooden side table with small framed picture(s) and a potted plant in the background
Sheer curtains over tall windows in the background
Man's dark suit jacket and tie; woman's knit brown turtleneck sweater and dark skirt
Small stud/pearl earring and ring as subtle wardrobe detail on the woman
lighting_notes: Warm, soft interior lighting consistent with a cozy evening living-room mood; key light is gentle and diffused across the felt-textured character skin/wool textures, with the lamp in the background acting as a motivated warm light source. The phone screens add small blue-white highlights on the characters' hands and faces, visually reinforcing the 'low battery / screen-addicted' theme. Background is intentionally shallow-focus/soft to keep contrast and detail concentrated on the two character faces in the foreground.
color_palette: warm skin/felt tan tones (character faces and hands)
black title cards with golden-yellow accent text and a yellow 'ticket' graphic for episode branding
visual_complexity_notes: Extremely minimal and deliberately static: one unchanging camera framing, one set, two characters, with background detail kept intentionally soft/out of focus. This stripped-down staging keeps all visual and comedic focus on the characters' deadpan expressions and phone-scrolling body language rather than on environment or camera movement, consistent with a stop-motion sitcom-style format built for quick, dialogue-driven gags.
